script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

EXT. CITY PARK - DAY

A gentle breeze rustles autumn leaves as CAROLINE (30s), a successful marketing executive, sits alone on a bench. She looks lost, her eyes distant as she stares at a tablet.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
(Caroline's voice)
I have it all... or so they say. A promising career, a beautiful apartment, a loving husband... yet something is missing.

INT. CAROLINE'S APARTMENT - LIVING ROOM - DAY

Caroline stands in front of her bookshelf, her eyes lingering on a dusty old book - "The Art of Painting." Her mother's voice echoes in her head.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
(Mother's voice)
You always loved to draw, Caroline. Don't let that passion fade away.

INT. CAFÉ - DAY

Caroline sits at a table, flipping through a sketchbook. Across the room, ROBERT (40s), a retired art teacher, notices her and approaches.

ROBERT
(kindly)
I see you're quite the artist.

CAROLINE
(startled, embarrassed)
Oh, just trying something new.

ROBERT
(smiling)
I believe in you, Caroline. You have a unique perspective that could make a wonderful addition to the art world.

INT. CAROLINE'S APARTMENT - STUDIO - NIGHT

Caroline sets up an easel and paints for the first time in years. The room is filled with the scent of turpentine and the sound of her brush against the canvas.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
The brush stroke felt natural in my hand. The colors blended together, creating something beautiful.

EXT. CITY PARK - DAY

Caroline stands in front of her easel, painting a landscape. Passersby pause to admire her work.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
I was scared. Excited. Nervous. But for the first time in years, I felt alive.

INT. ART GALLERY - EVENING

Caroline attends her first art exhibit. Her painting is displayed among others. A man, JAMES (30s), approaches her.

JAMES
(impressed)
Your painting is magnificent. I'd love to buy it.

CAROLINE
(surprised)
Thank you, but I'm not selling just yet. I want to see if I can create more.

INT. CAROLINE'S APARTMENT - LIVING ROOM - DAY

Caroline sits on her couch, holding her tablet and staring at her new painting. Her husband enters the room.

HUSBAND
(worried)
What's going on? You've been distant lately.

CAROLINE
(smiling)
I've decided to pursue my passion for painting. I've been offered the chance to exhibit my work at a local gallery.

HUSBAND
(proud)
I'm here for you, Caroline. Whatever you choose to do, I'll support you.

INT. ART GALLERY - EVENING

Caroline stands before a crowd, addressing her audience. Her painting is displayed prominently.

CAROLINE
(passionately)
I've spent years pursuing a successful career in marketing. But I've come to realize that my true calling is not in numbers and charts, but in the power of color and brush strokes. I'm here today to share my passion with you.

The room erupts in applause as Caroline steps down from the podium. She's finally found the missing piece of her life.

FADE OUT.
